content.overview: BNS s. 305 — Theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc. BNS restatement of IPC 380. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 380. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 305 is the rule on “Theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc”. The section provides that whoever commits theft—. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 305 exists so that “Theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Theft, snatching, extortion, robbery, dacoity, trust, cheating, mischief, trespass.

The provision in detail
305. Whoever commits theft—

(a) in any building, tent or vessel used as a human dwelling or used for the custody of property; or

(b) of any means of transport used for the transport of goods or passengers; or

(c) of any article or goods from any means of transport used for the transport of goods or passengers; or

(d) of idol or icon in any place of worship; or

(e) of any property of the Government or of a local authority,

shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. (a) in any building, tent or vessel used as a human dwelling or used for the custody of property; or
2. (b) of any means of transport used for the transport of goods or passengers; or
3. (c) of any article or goods from any means of transport used for the transport of goods or passengers; or
4. (d) of idol or icon in any place of worship; or
5. (e) of any property of the Government or of a local authority,
6. shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 305 (Theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 305 (Theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc), Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) (a) in any building, tent or vessel used as a human dwelling or used for the custody of property; or
   (2) (b) of any means of transport used for the transport of goods or passengers; or
   (3) (c) of any article or goods from any means of transport used for the transport of goods or passengers; or
   (4) (d) of idol or icon in any place of worship; or
   (5) (e) of any property of the Government or of a local authority,
   (6) shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 305 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 305 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
